newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks reduce gains at the close.
newsitem.headline: French stocks reduce gains at the close.

text.p: French shares closed higher on Monday but a last-minute bout of profit-taking eroded the early gains booked in a rebound to Friday's 2.26 percent slide on remarks by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 15.12 points or 0.67 percent at 2,255.84, while the CAC-40 futures contract rose to 2,259 from 2,239 on Friday's close.
The CAC-index hit a day high of 2,264.13 and a low of 2,250.29. The December future hit resistance at 2,270.
Volume was 4.8 billion francs, of which 3.2 billion in CAC-40 shares.
The market jumped at the opening after it realised that the Wall Street slide was less dramatic than it appeared on Friday and because the dollar and the Tokyo stock market held firm.

During the trading day, shares ran out of steam and were marking time ahead of the Wall Street opening. After the New York market's higher start, French shares took off again only to fall victim to profit-taking in the last half hour.
Dealers said market sentiment remained fragile and investors would remain sidelined to await the U.S. producer price index on Wednesday and consumer price index on Thursday.
The European Union summit in Dublin on monetary union, starting on Friday but preceded by a finance ministers' meeting on Thursday, is also keeping investors on their toes.

On Thursday, president Jacques Chirac will address the nation in a televised interview but he is not expected to make sweeping announcements. Another key date is December 17 when Bank of France governor Jean-Claude Trichet will host a news conference on monetary policy after a bank council meeting. That same day the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee will meet.
"It's a nice recovery," a dealer said about today's rise. But, he warned, "We could still hit another air pocket."

Club Mediterannee was the biggest riser, ending 8.80 percent higher at 344.90 on a speculative rise after key shareholders ended a 1990 pact, making the company more vulnerable to a takeover. Analysts at Paribas Capital Markets, SGE Delahaye and Dupont-Denant issued "buy" recommendations.
